'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**A [[Improvised explosive device|roadside bomb]] kills five civilians and injures three others in [[Tebessa Province]], [[Algeria]]. It is the deadliest attack on civilians in Algeria in recent years. In a separate incident, a militant is shot dead by the [[Algerian People's National Army|military]] in neighbouring  [[Khenchela Province]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/1/14/five-civilians-killed-in-algeria-bomb-blast-ministry-says (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Vatican Museums]] Director [[Barbara Jatta]], tells [[Vatican Radio]] it is necessary to extend the current closure of the Museums after having previously set 16 January as a possible date for re-opening. The current [[COVID-19 pandemic|Covid-19]] situation in Italy does not allow for certainties. Currently there is a seven-kilometre itinerary mapped out through the Vatican Museums for small numbers of visitors, in compliance with anti-Covid precautions. [https://www.vaticannews.va/en/vatican-city/news/2021-01/vatican-museums-reopening-february-barbara-jatta.html (''Vatican News'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
**[[President-elect of the United States|President-elect]] [[Joe Biden]] unveils a [[United States dollar|$]]1.9 trillion [[American Rescue Plan|relief package]] to bolster the [[Economy of the United States|United States economy]]. If passed in [[United States Congress|Congress]], the relief package will increase the direct payments from $600 to $2,000, an increase of $1,400. The plan to increase the direct payments to $2,000 was endorsed by Biden himself, outgoing [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]], and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-biden-stimulus/biden-to-unveil-plan-to-pump-19-trillion-into-pandemic-hit-economy-idUSKBN29J1B1 (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-55670801 (BBC News)]
*[[Automotive industry|Automotive]] manufacturer [[Toyota]] announces that it will pay a [[civil penalty]] of [[United States dollar|US$]]180 million minimum for violating [[United States vehicle emission standards]] by not reporting emissions defects to authorities. [https://www.news24.com/wheels/news/toyota-to-pay-180-million-to-settle-us-emissions-violations-govt-20210114 (AFP via News24)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]

******[[Governor of Maryland|Governor]] [[Larry Hogan]] announces that the [[Maryland|state]] will distribute the vaccine next week to teachers, people 75 or older, child care providers, residents of assisted living facilities, people in group homes, and high-risk inmates. ****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
*****The number of daily deaths in [[New York (state)|New York]] reaches 200 for the first time since May 12. [https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/coronavirus/2nd-uk-strain-cluster-found-on-long-island-nyc-nears-half-a-million-confirmed-covid-cases/2830879/ (WNBC-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Texas]]
*****[[Texas]] surpasses two million cases of COVID-19, becoming the second state to do so after [[California]]. [https://apnews.com/27afadf68ca44f5095be06fcb4d587ec (AP)]
*****[[Texas]] reaches past 1 million [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccinations]], becoming the first state to do so. [https://www.star-telegram.com/news/state/texas/article248512320.html (''Fort Worth Star-Telegram'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia]]
*****[[British Columbia]] reports their first case of a [[501.V2 variant|new variant]] of [[SARS-CoV-2]] from [[South Africa]]. [https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/bc-covid-19-south-african-uk-variant (Daily Hive)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[Prime Minister of France|Prime Minister]] [[Jean Castex]] announces that the [[Government of France|French government]] will impose a nationwide 6:00 p.m. curfew for at least 15 days beginning January 16 in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210114-covid-19-france-to-introduce-6pm-curfew-for-at-least-15-days-from-saturday (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
**** Germany reports a record 1,244 deaths in the past 24 hours, according to data from the [[Robert Koch Institute]], bringing the nationwide death toll to 43,881. [https://www.tagesschau.de/inland/rki-todesfaelle-neuinfektionen-101.html (Tagesschau)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports a new record for the second consecutive day, of 10,698 new daily cases, bringing the nationwide cumulative total of confirmed cases to 517,806. [https://covid19.min-saude.pt/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/318_DGS_boletim_20210114.pdf (DGS)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden]]
****[[Sweden]] reports a record 351 deaths in the past 24 hours and surpasses 10,000 deaths from [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.expressen.se/nyheter/coronaviruset/over-10-000-doda-fhms-besked-kommer-att-oka/ (''Expressen'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[President of Turkey|President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] receives the first dose of the [[CoronaVac]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] in a hospital in [[Ankara]] as [[Turkey]] begins its nationwide [[vaccination]] campaign. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/turkish-president-gets-covid-19-vaccine/2110204 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in China]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
*****[[China]] reports 138 new cases in the past 24 hours, the biggest single-day increase in more than 10 months, bringing the total number of cases since the beginning of the outbreak to 87,844. In addition, the country also reports its first death from COVID-19 since April, bringing the nationwide death toll to 4,635. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-01-14/china-reports-most-new-covid19-cases-in-more-than-10-months/13057984 (ABC Australia)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 11,557 new cases, bringing the nationwide total to 869,600 confirmed cases. [https://nasional.kompas.com/read/2021/01/14/16100471/update-bertambah-11557-kasus-covid-19-indonesia-capai-869600-orang (''Kompas'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 3,337 new cases, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 147,855. [https://www.theedgemarkets.com/article/covid19-malaysia-reports-3337-new-cases-15-deaths (The Edge Markets MY)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****The [[Food and Drug Administration (Philippines)|Food and Drug Administration]] approves the [[Pfizer]]–[[BioNTech]] [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] for emergency use in the country. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/philippines-clears-pfizer-covid-19-vaccine-emergency-use (Rappler)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Gambia]]
****[[The Gambia]] reports their first two cases of a [[Variant of Concern 202012/01|new variant]] of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] in a 34-year-old man who travelled to the [[United Kingdom]] and an 82-year-old woman who also tested positive. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-gambia/gambia-records-first-two-cases-of-uk-covid-19-variant-idUSKBN29J2BR (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nigeria]]
****The [[Federal Ministry of Education (Nigeria)|Federal Ministry of Education]] announces that [[Education in Nigeria|schools]] in [[Nigeria]] will reopen on January 18. Parents have appealed to the ministry to rescind the decision following a recent spike in COVID-19 cases. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2021-01/15/c_139669392.htm (Xinhua)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[Lineage B.1.1.248]]
***[[Secretary of State for Transport|British Transport Secretary]] [[Grant Shapps]] announces a ban on all travellers from [[South America]]n countries, as well as [[Portugal]], [[Panama]] and [[Cape Verde]] due to a new variant of [[SARS-CoV-2]] that was identified in [[Brazil]]. The ban will come into effect tomorrow at 4:00 a.m. [[GMT]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55666198 (BBC News)]
*[[Nuclear program of Iran]]
**The [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] (IAEA) says that [[Iran]] has informed them that it has begun installing equipment for the production of uranium metal, another violation in kind in response to Western violations of the [[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action]]. The IAEA says that Iran now has enough enriched uranium to make a [[nuclear weapon]], but still possesses less than it had before the deal was signed. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/un-watchdog-confirms-another-iranian-breach-of-nuclear-deal-production-deal-deal-watchdog-country-b1787238.html (''The Independent'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**The [[United States Attorney for the District of Columbia|U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia]] announces the arrest of [[Kevin Seefried]], a [[Delaware]] man who was seen [[Modern display of the Confederate battle flag|carrying]] the [[Flags of the Confederate States of America|Confederate flag]] during the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|storming]] of the [[United States Capitol]]. His son, Hunter Seefried, is also arrested. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/kevin-seefried-confederate-flag-capitol-riots-arrested/ (CBS News)]
**The [[United States Department of Justice|Department of Justice]] announces that Robert Sanford, a retired firefighter from [[Boothwyn, Pennsylvania|Boothwyn]], [[Pennsylvania]], has been arrested for allegedly throwing a fire extinguisher at [[United States Capitol Police|Capitol Police]] officers during the storming of the Capitol. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/2021/01/14/ex-firefighter-threw-extinguisher-capitol-police-riot/4160629001/ (''USA Today'')] 
*[[Crime in Australia]]
**[[Domestic violence in Australia]]
***A mother and three children are found dead in a suspected [[murder–suicide]] in [[Tullamarine, Victoria|Tullamarine]], [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]], in the second case of suspected [[familicide]] in Victoria in the past week. [https://www.news.com.au/national/victoria/crime/homicide-squad-investigates-after-four-people-found-dead-in-melbourne/news-story/46417da3d797ff5ca26141d2611e51ab (News.com.au)]
*[[Corruption in South Korea]]
**The [[Supreme Court of South Korea|Supreme Court]] upholds former [[President of South Korea|President]] [[Park Geun-hye]]'s 22-year prison sentence for [[corruption]]. [https://apnews.com/article/seoul-south-korea-park-geun-hye-elections-crime-6b7a2f8efc51edf2191a1d84dc4e1e97 (AP)]
*[[Flint water crisis]]
**Eight more [[Michigan]] officials are charged along with former [[Governor of Michigan|Governor]] [[Rick Snyder]] for their roles in the [[Flint, Michigan|Flint]] water crisis. Former health director Nick Lyon and former state medical executive Eden Wells are also charged with involuntary manslaughter in the deaths of nine people who contracted [[Legionnaires' disease]] during the crisis. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/8-former-michigan-officials-criminally-charged-along-ex-governor-flint-n1254286 (NBC News)] [https://apnews.com/article/environment-michigan-flint-rick-snyder-f5987ee1f56b62b6858052bb759f996f (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Ugandan general election]]
**Voters head to the polls to elect their next [[President of Uganda|president]] and [[Parliament of Uganda|parliament]]. The two main presidential candidates are incumbent President [[Yoweri Museveni]] and opposition activist and musician [[Bobi Wine]]. The election has been widely criticized as being unfair, with both the [[United States]] and [[European Union]] cancelling their observations of the election. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-55649467 (BBC News)]
